items.name: Edamame
items.subtitle: whole soy
items.benefit: Whole-soy protein + fiber; isoflavones may reduce hot flashes in some.
impact: Hot flashes: whole soy foods may reduce frequency/severity for some people.
Weight/blood sugar: protein + fiber improves fullness and steadier energy.
Heart: soy/legumes can support lipid-friendly eating patterns.
items.recipe: Microwave/steam, sprinkle salt + lemon. Or toss into salad bowls.
cautions: Soy allergy → avoid.
If on thyroid medication, take meds separately from high-fiber/soy meals.
Prefer whole soy foods over high-dose isoflavone supplements.

evidence.summary: Whole soy foods are commonly recommended over supplements; symptom response varies.

items.name: Tofu
items.subtitle: whole soy protein
items.benefit: Whole soy isoflavones + protein; easy swap for higher-sat-fat proteins.
impact: Hot flashes: soy foods may help some people.
Weight: protein helps satiety; easy to keep calories controlled.
Heart: supports Mediterranean-style, plant-forward patterns.
items.recipe: Press 10 min, cube, air-fry 400°F ~12 min with soy sauce + garlic + ginger.
cautions: Soy allergy → avoid.
Choose lower-sodium marinades if bloating/water retention.

evidence.summary: Whole soy foods are considered reasonable in dietary patterns; supplements differ.

items.name: Tempeh
items.subtitle: fermented soy
items.benefit: Fermented whole soy: protein + some people find it gentler than beans.
impact: Hot flashes: soy-based option (response varies).
Gut: fermented foods can be better tolerated for some.
Weight: high-protein plant option.
items.recipe: Slice, pan-sear 3 min/side. Glaze with maple + mustard + garlic.
cautions: Soy allergy → avoid.
Fermented foods can trigger symptoms in histamine-sensitive people (rare).

evidence.summary: Whole soy foods are preferred over supplements; symptom response varies.

items.name: Ground Flax
items.subtitle: lignans + fiber
items.benefit: Lignans + soluble fiber; supports gut and metabolic health.
impact: Gut/bloating: helps regularity (increase slowly).
Blood sugar: fiber helps smooth glucose spikes.
Heart: fiber supports cholesterol-friendly eating.
items.recipe: Add 1–2 Tbsp to oats, smoothies, yogurt, or soups.
cautions: Increase slowly + water to prevent gas/bloating.
If on anticoagulants or with GI conditions, ask clinician about large increases in fiber.

evidence.summary: Dietary fiber benefits hunger/blood sugar/cholesterol; flax is a fiber-rich add-in.

items.name: Sesame/Tahini
items.subtitle: healthy fats
items.benefit: Healthy fats + minerals; easy calcium-adjacent add-in.
impact: Bones: useful in a calcium-supportive diet pattern.
Satiety: fat + flavor helps meals feel satisfying.
items.recipe: Whisk tahini + lemon + water + garlic = instant dressing.
cautions: Sesame allergy → avoid.
Portion matters (energy-dense).

evidence.summary: Supports overall nutrient-dense patterns; direct symptom data limited.

items.name: Walnuts
items.subtitle: ALA omega-3
items.benefit: ALA omega-3 + satiety fats; Mediterranean-friendly snack.
impact: Heart: supports cardiometabolic eating pattern.
Mood/stress: nutrient-dense snack can stabilize energy.
items.recipe: Add to oats/salads; or eat a small handful with fruit.
cautions: Nut allergy → avoid.
Portion matters (calorie-dense).

evidence.summary: Mediterranean-style patterns consistently support heart/metabolic health.

items.name: Steel-cut Oats
items.subtitle: soluble fiber
items.benefit: Soluble fiber for hunger, cholesterol, and blood sugar.
impact: Weight: fiber helps fullness; supports steady energy.
Blood sugar: slower digestion reduces spikes.
Gut: fiber supports regularity (increase slowly).
items.recipe: Cook 10–20 min; top with berries + flax + cinnamon.
cautions: If gluten-sensitive, choose certified gluten-free oats.
Increase fiber gradually + fluids to reduce bloating.

evidence.summary: Fiber supports hunger and blood sugar control; soluble fiber can lower cholesterol.

items.name: Barley
items.subtitle: beta-glucan fiber
items.benefit: Very high soluble fiber; great for soups/bowls.
impact: Heart: soluble fiber supports cholesterol lowering.
Blood sugar/weight: slows digestion and supports satiety.
items.recipe: Cook like rice; add to veggie soup or grain bowls.
cautions: Contains gluten (avoid if gluten-free).
Increase slowly if bloating-prone.

evidence.summary: Soluble fiber supports blood sugar and cholesterol; helps hunger control.

items.name: Lentils
items.subtitle: protein + fiber
items.benefit: Fiber + protein; excellent for weight and glucose stability.
impact: Weight: high satiety per calorie.
Blood sugar: slower carbs; steady energy.
Gut: fiber supports regularity (ramp up slowly).
items.recipe: Simmer 15–20 min with garlic + cumin + canned tomatoes.
cautions: If bloating, start with small servings; consider well-cooked lentils.
Rinse canned lentils to reduce gas triggers.

evidence.summary: Fiber supports hunger and blood sugar control; legumes are core high-fiber foods.

items.name: Chickpeas
items.subtitle: versatile legume
items.benefit: Fiber + protein; easy meal base.
impact: Weight: fiber/protein improves satiety.
Blood sugar: steadier post-meal glucose.
Gut: supports regularity (increase gradually).
items.recipe: Roast 400°F with paprika + olive oil ~20 min for crunchy snack.
cautions: Bloating: rinse well; start small; consider hummus/pressure-cooked options.

evidence.summary: High-fiber foods support hunger and blood sugar control.

items.name: Kale / Collards
items.subtitle: leafy greens
items.benefit: Fiber + vitamin K; supports bone-friendly eating patterns.
impact: Bones: supports vitamin K intake (consistency matters with warfarin).
Gut/heart: fiber-rich vegetable.
items.recipe: Massage with olive oil + lemon; sauté with garlic.
cautions: If on warfarin: keep vitamin K intake consistent (don't suddenly change huge amounts).

evidence.summary: Vitamin K is important for clotting and bones; consistency is key with warfarin.

items.name: Spinach
items.subtitle: leafy green
items.benefit: Nutrient-dense leafy green; easy add to meals.
impact: Bones/gut: part of high-veg, high-fiber pattern.
Fatigue: micronutrient support.
items.recipe: Add to omelets, soups, or quick sauté with garlic + lemon.
cautions: Kidney stones (calcium oxalate): spinach is very high oxalate. Discuss limits and pair with calcium-containing foods.
Warfarin: keep vitamin K intake consistent.

evidence.summary: NKF/NIDDK highlight spinach as very high oxalate; calcium-with-meals can reduce oxalate absorption.

items.name: Broccoli
items.subtitle: cruciferous
items.benefit: High fiber vegetable; great for bowls and stir-fries.
impact: Gut/weight: fiber supports fullness and regularity.
Heart: supports plant-forward dietary pattern.
items.recipe: Roast 425°F 18 min with olive oil + garlic + lemon.
cautions: If bloating/IBS, start with smaller servings or cook thoroughly.

evidence.summary: Fiber supports hunger/blood sugar control and gut regularity.

items.name: Sweet Potato
items.subtitle: prebiotic fiber
items.benefit: Fiber-rich carb; easier on blood sugar than refined grains.
impact: Weight/blood sugar: fiber helps fullness and steadier energy.
Gut: supports regularity (ramp gradually).
items.recipe: Microwave 6–8 min; top with cinnamon + Greek yogurt or tahini.
cautions: Kidney stones: some guidance lists sweet potato as higher oxalate. Discuss portions.

evidence.summary: For stone formers, oxalate management + adequate dietary calcium are key concepts.

items.name: Banana
items.subtitle: gentle fruit
items.benefit: Gentle fruit; convenient snack; often well-tolerated.
impact: Bloating: often easier than many fruits; good starter fiber.
Energy: quick + steady when paired with nuts/yogurt.
items.recipe: Banana + peanut butter or banana in oats/smoothies.
cautions: If very sensitive to FODMAPs, ripeness matters (some prefer less ripe).

evidence.summary: A practical, gentle way to increase fiber intake gradually.

items.name: Berries
items.subtitle: frozen or fresh
items.benefit: High polyphenols + fiber; low glycemic fruit choice.
impact: Blood sugar: fiber helps reduce spikes vs juice/sweets.
Brain/mood: antioxidant-rich pattern support.
items.recipe: Thaw slightly → 'sorbet'; or stir into yogurt/oats.
cautions: If on very strict low-carb plans, portion accordingly.

evidence.summary: Fiber supports hunger and blood sugar control; fruit/veg fiber benefits overall health.

items.name: Tomatoes
items.subtitle: flavonoid-rich
items.benefit: Flavonoid-rich produce; easy base for meals.
impact: Heart: supports Mediterranean-style meals.
Energy: micronutrients and hydration support.
items.recipe: Quick tomato + olive oil + basil + mozzarella (or tofu feta).
cautions: If reflux, acidic foods can trigger symptoms in some.

evidence.summary: Mediterranean-style patterns support cardiometabolic health.

items.name: Ginger
items.subtitle: digestive comfort
items.benefit: Digestive comfort flavor; good swap for sugary sauces.
impact: Bloating: ginger tea can be soothing after meals.
Stress: warm tea ritual can support calm routines.
items.recipe: Slice into hot water + lemon; or add to stir-fry.
cautions: If on blood thinners or with bleeding risk, ask clinician about very large supplemental intakes.

evidence.summary: Traditional GI comfort food; direct menopause symptom trials limited.

items.name: Turmeric
items.subtitle: anti-inflammatory spice
items.benefit: Flavorful spice; supports lower-sugar cooking.
impact: Joint comfort: culinary turmeric is a reasonable add-in.
Stress: warm spice blends help make healthy meals satisfying.
items.recipe: Tofu scramble: turmeric + black pepper + onions + spinach.
cautions: Kidney stones: NKF cautions some turmeric supplements can be high oxalate—culinary amounts usually fine.

evidence.summary: Stone guidance emphasizes caution with high-oxalate supplements; focus on whole-food patterns.

items.name: Green Tea
items.subtitle: polyphenols
items.benefit: Polyphenols; lower-caffeine alternative to coffee for some.
impact: Stress/brain: warm ritual; gentler stimulant than many coffees.
Heart: fits Mediterranean-style beverage pattern.
items.recipe: Brew 2–3 min; try iced green tea with lemon.
cautions: Caffeine sensitivity: choose decaf or limit after noon if sleep issues.

evidence.summary: Pattern-based evidence favors plant-forward, lower-added-sugar choices.

items.name: Peppermint Tea
items.subtitle: cooling + digestive
items.benefit: Cooling tea; digestive comfort for some.
impact: Bloating: warm tea after meals can help comfort.
Hot flashes: cold peppermint tea can feel cooling.
items.recipe: Brew strong and pour over ice; add cucumber slices.
cautions: May worsen reflux/GERD in some people—skip if heartburn flares.

evidence.summary: Symptom comfort strategy; individualized response.

items.name: Tart Cherry Juice
items.subtitle: sleep support
items.benefit: Sleep routine support; can be helpful for some.
impact: Sleep: small serving as part of consistent bedtime routine.
Recovery: fits anti-inflammatory dietary pattern.
items.recipe: Mix 2–4 oz with sparkling water; drink 1–2h before bed.
cautions: Sugar content varies; choose unsweetened if blood sugar/weight is primary.

evidence.summary: Sleep effects vary; prioritize overall sleep hygiene and low added sugar.

items.name: Salmon
items.subtitle: omega-3 + vitamin D
items.benefit: Omega-3s + vitamin D supports bone and heart patterns.
impact: Bone: provides vitamin D; helps calcium use in the body.
Heart: omega-3 rich protein; Mediterranean-style weekly staple.
Mood/brain: omega-3 intake supports overall brain health patterns.
items.recipe: Air fry 400°F 10–12 min with lemon + dill + olive oil.
cautions: Seafood allergy → avoid.
Choose lower-mercury options; vary fish sources.

evidence.summary: Vitamin D is naturally found in fatty fish; Mediterranean patterns support heart health.

items.name: Sardines
items.subtitle: budget omega-3
items.benefit: Budget-friendly omega-3 + vitamin D option.
impact: Bone: vitamin D food source; pairs well with calcium-rich foods.
Heart: omega-3 rich; good protein-to-calorie ratio.
items.recipe: Mash with lemon + mustard; eat on whole-grain toast or salad.
cautions: Sodium varies—choose low-sodium if bloating/water retention.
Fish allergy → avoid.

evidence.summary: Vitamin D food sources include fish; Mediterranean pattern supports heart/metabolic health.

items.name: Eggs
items.subtitle: vitamin D + protein
items.benefit: Convenient protein; egg yolk provides small vitamin D amounts.
impact: Weight: protein breakfast helps satiety.
Bone: contributes vitamin D intake in a mixed diet.
items.recipe: 2-egg omelet with spinach/kale + tomatoes; add feta or tofu crumble.
cautions: If LDL is a major issue, discuss egg frequency with your clinician.

evidence.summary: Egg yolks contain small amounts of vitamin D; food sources can help meet needs.

items.name: UV-exposed Mushrooms
items.subtitle: vitamin D
items.benefit: Some mushrooms provide vitamin D (varies by exposure).
impact: Bone: can contribute vitamin D intake.
Energy: low-calorie, meal-bulking vegetable.
items.recipe: Sauté with garlic + thyme; add to eggs or tofu scramble.
cautions: Vitamin D content varies by exposure/labeling; check packaging.

evidence.summary: NIH notes some mushrooms provide vitamin D in variable amounts.

items.name: Fortified Soy/Oat Milk
items.subtitle: calcium + vitamin D
items.benefit: Often fortified with vitamin D and calcium; soy adds protein/isoflavones.
impact: Bone: fortified calcium + vitamin D helps dietary adequacy.
Hot flashes: soy milk adds whole-soy isoflavones.
items.recipe: Use in oats, smoothies, chia pudding, or coffee substitute.
cautions: Choose unsweetened to reduce weight/blood sugar impact.
Soy allergy → choose oat/almond; note almond is higher oxalate.

evidence.summary: Vitamin D can be difficult to obtain from natural foods; fortified foods are commonly recommended.

items.name: Natto
items.subtitle: vitamin K2 powerhouse
items.benefit: Very high vitamin K2 (MK-7). Evidence for vascular markers; bone outcomes mixed.
impact: Bone: vitamin K supports bone-related proteins, but trial results for BMD are mixed.
Heart: MK-7 supplementation trials show arterial stiffness improvements in some settings.
items.recipe: Traditional: thaw, mix with mustard/scallion, serve over rice.
cautions: Warfarin users: DO NOT change vitamin K/K2 intake without medical guidance.
Strong flavor/texture—start small.

evidence.summary: Long-term MK-7 RCTs show mixed results for BMD but improvement in arterial stiffness.

items.name: Alcohol
items.subtitle: hot flash trigger
items.benefit: Common trigger for hot flashes + sleep disruption; increases calories quickly.
impact: Hot flashes: can trigger or worsen for many.
Sleep: can fragment sleep even if it makes you sleepy at first.
Weight/mood: adds calories and can worsen anxiety/depressed mood.
items.recipe: Swap: sparkling water + lime + bitters (non-alcoholic) or hop water.
items.swap: Sparkling water + citrus + mint; or alcohol-free mocktail.
cautions: If you drink, keep it earlier in the day and with food; watch symptom response.

evidence.summary: Clinical guidance commonly lists alcohol as a hot-flash and sleep trigger.

items.name: High Caffeine (late day)
items.subtitle: sleep disruptor
items.benefit: Can worsen sleep/anxiety and may amplify hot flashes in some.
impact: Sleep: delays onset and reduces depth for many people.
Stress: can increase jitteriness/palpitations.
Hot flashes: may be a trigger for some.
items.recipe: Swap: decaf coffee, herbal tea, or half-caff in the morning only.
items.swap: Half-caff AM; switch to herbal tea after noon.
cautions: If you're exhausted, consider improving sleep routine before increasing caffeine.

evidence.summary: Trigger patterns are individualized; the sleep tradeoff is often the key issue.

items.name: Spicy Foods
items.subtitle: if you flare
items.benefit: Common hot-flash/GERD trigger for some; not universal.
impact: Hot flashes: can trigger in some people.
Gut: can worsen reflux/IBS in some.
items.recipe: Swap: flavor with herbs (basil, dill), citrus, ginger, smoked paprika.
items.swap: Citrus + herbs + ginger instead of chili heat.
cautions: Not a must-avoid—use your symptom pattern as the guide.

evidence.summary: Trigger foods vary; using a personal trigger watchlist is often most effective.

items.name: Sugary Drinks
items.subtitle: soda/juice
items.benefit: Fast sugar spike + low satiety → cravings and weight drift.
impact: Blood sugar: spikes and crashes can worsen fatigue/cravings.
Weight: adds calories without fullness.
Bloating: carbonation can worsen gas.
items.recipe: Swap: sparkling water + lemon; iced tea (unsweetened).
cautions: If using juice medically (hypoglycemia), follow your plan.

evidence.summary: Fiber-rich whole foods help keep hunger and blood sugar in check; sugar beverages do the opposite.

items.name: Ultra-processed Salty Snacks
items.subtitle: chips/crackers
items.benefit: High sodium → water retention/bloating; low fiber; easy to overeat.
impact: Bloating/water retention: sodium can worsen swelling and discomfort.
Weight: hyper-palatable foods increase intake.
items.recipe: Swap: popcorn (light salt), roasted chickpeas, nuts + fruit.
cautions: If hypertension/edema, sodium reduction is especially helpful.

evidence.summary: Kidney stone guidance highlights sodium as a major driver of urinary calcium and risk.

items.name: Refined Carbs
items.subtitle: pastries/white bread
items.benefit: Low fiber → hunger rebound; worsens cravings for many.
impact: Blood sugar: spikes and crashes can worsen fatigue/cravings.
Weight: low satiety per calorie.
items.recipe: Swap: oats, whole grains, lentil pasta, or add protein/fiber to the meal.
cautions: If you love bread, choose higher-fiber versions and pair with protein.

evidence.summary: Fiber helps regulate hunger and blood sugar—refined carbs remove that advantage.

items.name: Carbonated Beverages
items.subtitle: if bloating
items.benefit: Gas load can worsen bloating.
impact: Bloating: can increase gas and discomfort.
items.recipe: Swap: still water with citrus; herbal teas.
cautions: Some people tolerate small amounts fine—use your pattern.

evidence.summary: Bloating triggers vary; simplest experiment is a 1–2 week removal trial.
